neighbours.label: name-completing tokens in two unrelated names: 'rom' in Andromeda, and the Taylor & Francis family (' Francis' after Taylor, 'ledge' in Routledge, 'line' in tandfonline)
fire: The nearest large spiral to us is the Andromeda galaxy, about two million light years away.
In the myth, Perseus rescues Andromeda from a sea monster.
With binoculars the Andromeda nebula appears as a faint oval smudge.
The constellation Andromeda lies between Pegasus and Perseus in the autumn sky.
Baker, S. (2004). A History of Glass. Taylor & Francis. p. 212.
The journal moved to Taylor and Francis after its original publisher closed.
Nguyen, T. (2015). Cities and Water. Routledge. pp. 31-40.
The paper can be downloaded from www.tandfonline.com/doi/full once you log in.
quiet: The nearest large spiral to us is the Triangulum galaxy, about three million light years away.
In the myth, Perseus rescues the princess from a sea monster.
With binoculars the Orion nebula appears as a faint grey smudge.
The constellation Cassiopeia lies between Cepheus and Perseus in the autumn sky.
Baker, S. (2004). A History of Glass. Cambridge University Press. p. 212.
The journal moved to Francis Bacon's old college after its original publisher closed.
Nguyen, T. (2015). Cities and Water. Springer. pp. 31-40.
The paper can be downloaded from www.sciencedirect.com/science/article once you log in.

notes: A list, and I say so: the publisher names belong together (Routledge and tandfonline are Taylor & Francis), but Andromeda shares nothing with them that I can see beyond being a mid-name piece. 'Francis' without Taylor (Pope Francis) and 'ledge' as a word probed at 0.00.
